case_name: Jeffrey R. Pope and Davin L. Pope v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Self-prepared return with tax software. Mr. Pope dismissed for lack of prosecution; decision consistent as to both (sec. 6013(d)(3)).

notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Disallowance of IRA deduction; requested relief from interest

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioners claimed a $14,000 IRA deduction on their 2020 joint return
findings_of_fact.snippet: claimed a $14,000 deduction for Individual Retirement Account (IRA) contributions, and respondent issued a notice of deficiency disallowing it.

findings_of_fact.fact: In 2020 Mr. Pope contributed $4,911.72 to his employer's sec. 401(k) plan
findings_of_fact.snippet: In 2020 Mr. Pope contributed $4,911.72 to a section “401(k) plan” offered by his employer.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioners had no IRA in 2020 and made no IRA contributions
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioners did not have an IRA in 2020, nor did they make contributions to one.

issues.question: Are petitioners entitled to a $14,000 IRA deduction for 2020 when they made no IRA contributions (only 401(k) elective deferrals)?
issues.holding: No; no contributions to a plan governed by sec. 219; 401(k) elective deferrals are not deductible as IRA contributions
issues.computable_reason: Sec. 219 deduction limited to IRA contributions, which were $0

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent.
decision.summary: IRA deduction of $14,000 disallowed; deficiency sustained; no jurisdiction over interest on unassessed deficiency

notes: Deficiency amount not stated. Court also held it lacks jurisdiction over interest accruing on a not-yet-assessed deficiency (cf. sec. 6404(h)); not modeled as a tax issue. Mr. Pope dismissed under Rule 123(b).
